messages:
Maria L.: Opening an Azure support case for multi-region quota lifts — need NVv4 GPU SKUs + extra NAT gateway public IPs + higher NIC count on a new subscription. Case created: 200987654321. Requesting help coordinating with TAM.
Kevin B.: thanks — which regions and what's the subscription id?
Maria L.: regions: West US 3 (uswest3) and Southeast Asia (southeastasia). Sub: `sub-0a1b2c3d4e5f`.
Priya S.: what's the expected scale? how many GPUs and NAT IPs are we asking for?
Maria L.: initial target = 24 NVv4 (mishmash of 8x and 4x pods), plus 40 extra public IPs (NAT gateway) across two vnets. If they approve, we'll ramp another 48 in 2 weeks.
Devon R.: ran into quota block when provisioning a test cluster earlier. here's the az cli error:
```
(Provisioning) Code: QuotaExceeded
Message: Quota 'Total Regional vCPU' for region 'southeastasia' was exceeded.\nDetails: Requested: 96, Current: 64, Limit: 64
```
Devon R.: also saw `NetworkInterfacesLimitExceeded` when trying to attach many pods to the VMSS.
Kevin B.: cc @OpsOncall — this will impact canary runs and staging autoscale. We should request temporary burst first, not full permanent increase.
Maria L.: Agreed. Filed primary ask as temporary burst for 30 days while Microsoft validates capacity, then permanent increase if perf looks good. Noted in case 200987654321.
AzureSupportBot: Support case 200987654321 updated by Microsoft Support (agent: R. Tan). Current status: "Under review by quotas team". SLA: 72 hours.
Priya S.: do we have a cost estimate? GPUs in southeastasia are pricier; if they only allow ephemeral burst we might pay premium.
Maria L.: rough sticker: +$12k/mo if permanent. For 30-day burst maybe ~$6k one-time based on on-demand. I'll put numbers in the ticket comment.
Devon R.: adding the exact ARM template snippet that failed — maybe quota request needs separate resource-type increments (vmFamily / vCPU / NIC / PublicIPs):
```
{
  "type": "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets",
  "sku": { "name": "Standard_NV48ads_A10_v5" },
  "properties": { /* ... */ }
}
```
Kevin B.: Microsoft asked for the subscription's billing contact and a short workload justification. Maria, can you paste the justification here so I can add to the internal approval thread?
Maria L.: justification pasted to case: "Redwood inference: short-lived canary + production reserve for low-latency inference. Need NVv4 for quantized model latency testing and throughput validation. Will route traffic gradually; require NAT IPs for egress / monitoring. Expected initial traffic 1000 qps across clusters."
OpsOncall: FYI — we should add a fallback plan: pin critical routes to a smaller SKU in another region if quota not approved in time.
Priya S.: also flagging subnet IP exhaustion potential — need to expand subnet sizes in both vnets if NIC count increases.
AzureSupportBot: Support case 200987654321 comment: "Please confirm billing contact email and attach workload justification document. Quotas team may require subscription validation."
Maria L.: I attached the justification PDF and billing contact: infra-billing@redwood.ai. Replied asking for tentative timeline and whether TAM can pre-approve capacity for a 30-day burst.
Kevin B.: Microsoft support just provided a provisional case number for escalation to TAM: ESC-AZ-334455. They're routing to US engineering quota team because NVv4 inventory is regional.
Devon R.: any workaround for immediate tests? We could spin smaller A100-equivalent in uswest2 but network latency to our storage will increase. Tradeoff call.
Maria L.: For immediate canary we'll do 8 nodes in uswest2 (already available), and keep the rest queued until approval. Not ideal but unblocks CI.
OpsOncall: marking action items: 1) Maria — follow up with TAM and push for 48-hour review. 2) Kevin — update canary scheduling to use uswest2 fallback. 3) Devon — confirm subnet sizes and post updated ARM templates.
Priya S.: thanks — also check quotas for Public IP per NAT gateway vs per subscription; Azure sometimes enforces per-zone limits.
AzureSupportBot: Case 200987654321 status update: "Quotas team requested subscription validation documents. Next update expected within 48-72 hours." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Maria L.: will ping again in 24h. If no movement, escalate through our TAM contact. :+1:
Kevin B.: thanks all. will sync with release manager and adjust canary windows. :thumbsup:
